findings.text: non-blocking: the assertion the commit adds, `assert "## Selected documentation conventions for this name" not in rendered`, is an exact duplicate of the pre-existing assertion two lines below at 67. The repair's only new coverage in this test is the `conventions_context_for(UNSELECTED) is None` line; the duplicated block renders as a second check that no longer exists in intent, and the reader cannot tell which of the two was meant to say something else.

non-blocking: `_routed_to_refinement` is the test file's own re-implementation of the acceptance predicate (`score < min_score or review_holds`) rather than a call to the owner at imas_codex/standard_names/review/holds.py:263 `docs_accepted`, which returns `score >= min_score and not open_holds(...)`. The two move together by convention, not by construction: a future change to the production predicate that keeps those two terms (a new quorum or link gate) leaves the helper and the four tests resting on it green. The added `_held_for(persisted, "registry_conformance")` assertions at 183, 199 and 215 are independent of the helper and do guard production output.

non-blocking: the stage the test asserts on (`assert stage == "reviewed"`) is produced by a test-local `persist` stub that this commit rewrote to add the `review_holds` term. The assertion therefore measures the stub's model of `persist_reviewed_docs`, not the function, and stays green if production regressed to score-only acceptance. The added `assert [hold["kind"] for hold in persisted["review_holds"]] == ["banned_prose"]` is independent, because `persisted` is the kwargs the real worker hands to persistence.

non-blocking: `_PROTECTION_QUERY_LINE` pins a raw line number into imas_codex/standard_names/protection.py, and a line-number pin is what broke when an unrelated guard shifted the literal from 100 to 99. The content guard at line 43 (`assert "catalog_merge_commit_sha" in query`) is the right instrument; the line pin adds brittleness without adding discrimination, and an ast walk selecting the `query(...)` literal that carries that identifier would survive the next insertion. Pre-existing shape, re-pinned rather than re-anchored.

non-blocking: the id table cites `review/holds.py:266` as the acceptance predicate; 266 is the docstring line and the `return score >= min_score and not open_holds(name_id, "docs", graph=graph)` is at 267. The statement is correct and the anchor is off by one, in a fragment whose own anchor-check section is about exactly this failure.
